methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multicenter cohort of 187 HCC patients treated 2014-2024 across 8 Italian centers. Clear inclusion/exclusion criteria applied; patient selection biased toward complete follow-up datasets (14 patients excluded due to missing imaging). Stratified analysis by treatment approach (superselective vs. lobar). Statistical methods appropriate: Chi-square tests with Bonferroni correction, logistic regression for response predictors. However, no randomization, no propensity matching between groups; potential allocation bias. Some confounding variables uncontrolled.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort (LoE 2b) in routine HCC clinical practice. DSM-TACE with EmboCept is emerging TACE modality; study evaluates real-world efficacy and safety beyond formal RCTs. Procedural selectivity (superselective vs. lobar) showed differential efficacy at intermediate follow-up (ORR 53.8% vs. 26.4% at 3-6 months). Relevant to HCC treatment decision-making but lacks prospective design and formal comparative evidence.

reporting_quality.justification: Study presents multicenter retrospective data with baseline characteristics (Table 1-2), safety data (Table 3-4), and efficacy outcomes (Table 5-6). CTCAE grading for adverse events applied; mRECIST criteria for response assessment documented. However, no formal reporting standard (STROBE/CONSORT) explicitly applied. Data collection via CRF across centers but with heterogeneous follow-up imaging protocols. No data repository or code availability mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: DSM-TACE is established modality (known advantages: short embolization, liver sparing). Study applies existing techniques to real-world Italian cohort. Procedural comparison (superselective vs. lobar) provides practical guidance but represents incremental contribution. Prior literature variability (ORR 39-84%) acknowledged; present study (70% at 1 month, declining to 13.5% at 9-12 months) broadly consistent with prior reports. Limited novel insight into mechanisms or unexpected findings.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is readable with clear introduction contextualizing TACE evolution and DSM-TACE rationale. Methods describe procedural technique and statistical approaches. Results systematically present safety, efficacy overall, and per-patient/per-nodule comparisons. However, presentation is somewhat dense; some key results (e.g., significance loss after BCLC stratification, Table 6) not adequately emphasized. Discussion appropriately acknowledges limitations and prior comparisons.

key_strengths: Large real-world multicenter cohort (187 patients, 334 nodules) from 8 Italian high-volume interventional radiology centers over 10-year period
Excellent safety profile: no grade ≥3 adverse events, no procedure-related deaths; comparable PES rates between approaches (29.2% overall, 32.7% lobar vs. 17.6% superselective, p=0.14)

Clear procedural comparison showing advantage of superselective approach at intermediate follow-up: 3-6 month ORR 53.8% vs. 26.4% (p=0.009); per-nodule analysis confirms advantage (66.7% vs. 31.3%, p=0.0008)
Comprehensive reporting of baseline characteristics and stratification by BCLC stage; logistic regression identifies predictors of response
key_concerns: Retrospective design with selection bias: 14 patients (7%) excluded due to missing follow-up imaging; preferentially includes patients with complete datasets
Lack of randomization or matching between superselective and lobar groups; potential confounding by indication (operator preference, tumor distribution)
Significance of superselective advantage is lost after BCLC stratification (Table 6, p=0.05); suggests effect may be confounded by disease stage
Declining efficacy over time (ORR 70% at 1 month → 13.5% at 9-12 months) not explained; limited long-term outcome data beyond 12 months
No data sharing or code availability; limited reproducibility of analyses
Study scope narrowly focused on single TACE modality (DSM); no comparative effectiveness vs. other TACE platforms (cTACE, DEB-TACE)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid real-world safety and efficacy data for DSM-TACE but retrospective design, selection bias, and confounding by indication limit strength of comparative findings. Appropriate for Tier 4 (routine clinical case series with practical utility but limited evidence hierarchy). Accept with minor revisions addressing allocation bias and BCLC-stratified analysis.
